stem: In cystic fibrosis, what defect explains why a corrector is needed for the common F508 mutation?

options.text: A defect caused by acute infection alone
A problem limited to exercise tolerance

explanation: A processing defect is the correct answer. The common F508 mutation is a Class II CFTR defect, so the main problem is abnormal protein processing rather than channel opening.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because channel opening defects are Class III CFTR mutations, not the F508 mutation described here.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the F508 mutation is a Class II CFTR defect with abnormal protein processing, which is why a corrector is needed.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because acute infection is not the underlying CFTR mutation defect.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because fat-soluble vitamin deficiency is a consequence of cystic fibrosis, not the molecular defect itself.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because reduced exercise tolerance is a clinical feature, not the CFTR processing defect being tested.
